explanation.text: The Logic: Trade-based money laundering is defined as the process of disguising the proceeds of crime and moving value through the use of trade transactions in an attempt to legitimise their illicit origins. It is one of three broad methods criminals use to move money alongside financial system abuse and physical cash movement. The Trap: TBML specifically involves TRADE transactions (imports/exports of goods and services), not stock-market trading, crypto exchanges, or informal value transfer systems - those are different ML methods. Note: The three broad ML methods are: (1) the financial system (wire transfers, cheques); (2) physical cash movement (couriers, smuggling); and (3) trade (e.g., over/under-invoicing, phantom shipments).
